context: The page says confirm only irreversible actions and use a toast with Undo for the rest. The Confirm variant says it is for an action that can be undone or that others will see. ConfirmDialog draws a primary button (Confirm) or, with destructive, a danger one.

options.text: Confirm is for actions that reach other people or are costly to reverse (publish, send, share). Destructive is for irreversible loss. A private undoable action gets a toast with Undo.

render.jsx: h(P.Inline, null, h(P.Text, null, '3 assets moved to the trash.'), h(P.Button, { size: 'sm' }, 'Undo'))

options.label: Only irreversible actions
options.text: Every confirmation is for irreversible actions; the Confirm variant text is rewritten and publishing or sending never asks.

render.caption: Only the irreversible case asks
render.jsx: h(function Demo(){ const [o, s] = React.useState(false); const c = () => s(false); return h(React.Fragment, null, h(P.Button, { onClick: () => s(true) }, 'Open: Delete 3 assets?'), h(P.ConfirmDialog, { open: o, title: 'Delete 3 assets?', message: 'This cannot be undone.', confirmLabel: 'Delete', destructive: true, onConfirm: c, onCancel: c })); })
